Description: Average acceleration along the medio-lateral axis over the 10-second window
Clinical Relevance: Reflects the average medio-lateral body displacement; deviations from zero indicate asymmetric movement patterns

Description: Average acceleration along the vertical axis over the 10-second window
Clinical Relevance: Reflects gravitational offset and average vertical body displacement during walking

Description: Average acceleration along the antero-posterior axis over the 10-second window
Clinical Relevance: Captures average forward progression dynamics during gait

Description: Average resultant acceleration magnitude across all three axes
Clinical Relevance: Represents the overall average movement intensity; increases with walking speed

Description: Dispersion of medio-lateral acceleration values around the mean
Clinical Relevance: Elevated values indicate increased lateral instability or asymmetric arm swing

Description: Dispersion of vertical acceleration values around the mean
Clinical Relevance: Sensitive to stride-to-stride amplitude irregularity; among the top-ranked features for gait classification

Description: Dispersion of antero-posterior acceleration values around the mean
Clinical Relevance: Captures variability in the forward propulsion component of gait

Description: Dispersion of the resultant acceleration magnitude
Clinical Relevance: Overall signal variability; higher in fast or irregular walking patterns

Description: Squared dispersion of medio-lateral acceleration
Clinical Relevance: Amplifies large deviations in lateral motion; useful for detecting asymmetry

Description: Squared dispersion of vertical acceleration
Clinical Relevance: Captures magnitude of vertical oscillation variability across strides

Description: Squared dispersion of antero-posterior acceleration
Clinical Relevance: Reflects consistency of the forward propulsion across steps

Description: Squared dispersion of resultant acceleration magnitude
Clinical Relevance: Top-ranked feature for gait classification; captures overall stride-to-stride motion variability

Description: Peak-to-peak amplitude of medio-lateral acceleration
Clinical Relevance: Reflects the total excursion of lateral body sway during the window

Description: Peak-to-peak amplitude of vertical acceleration
Clinical Relevance: Reflects the total vertical oscillation amplitude per walking window

Description: Peak-to-peak amplitude of antero-posterior acceleration
Clinical Relevance: Captures the amplitude of the forward-backward acceleration cycle

Description: Peak-to-peak amplitude of resultant acceleration
Clinical Relevance: Total dynamic range of movement intensity within the window

Description: Peak value of medio-lateral acceleration
Clinical Relevance: Represents the maximum lateral impulse during the window

Description: Peak value of vertical acceleration
Clinical Relevance: Represents the maximum vertical impact force proxy during heel strike

Description: Peak value of antero-posterior acceleration
Clinical Relevance: Represents the maximum forward propulsion impulse

Description: Peak resultant acceleration across all axes
Clinical Relevance: Reflects the highest movement intensity event within the window

Description: Minimum value of medio-lateral acceleration
Clinical Relevance: Captures the maximum lateral deceleration or opposing motion

Description: Minimum value of vertical acceleration
Clinical Relevance: Captures the lowest vertical acceleration point in the gait cycle

Description: Minimum value of antero-posterior acceleration
Clinical Relevance: Captures the maximum braking phase in the forward direction

Description: Minimum resultant acceleration across all axes
Clinical Relevance: Reflects the quietest movement phase within the window

Description: Lower quartile of the magnitude distribution
Clinical Relevance: Represents the intensity level below which 25% of motion samples fall

Description: Median of the magnitude distribution
Clinical Relevance: Robust central tendency of movement intensity; less sensitive to outlier peaks

Description: Upper quartile of the magnitude distribution
Clinical Relevance: Represents the intensity level below which 75% of motion samples fall

Full Name: Coefficient of variation of acceleration magnitude
Description: Normalized variability of the magnitude signal
Clinical Relevance: Allows cross-subject comparison of motion variability independent of absolute intensity level

Full Name: Root mean square of X-axis acceleration
Description: Effective amplitude of medio-lateral acceleration
Clinical Relevance: Combines mean and variability into a single energy-related descriptor

Full Name: Root mean square of Y-axis acceleration
Description: Effective amplitude of vertical acceleration
Clinical Relevance: Relates to the energetic cost of vertical oscillation during walking

Full Name: Root mean square of Z-axis acceleration
Description: Effective amplitude of antero-posterior acceleration
Clinical Relevance: Reflects propulsive effort in the walking direction

Full Name: Root mean square of acceleration magnitude
Description: Effective overall signal amplitude across all axes
Clinical Relevance: Proportional to the mechanical power exerted during walking; increases with gait speed

Description: Mean of the resultant jerk magnitude computed as the temporal derivative of acceleration
Clinical Relevance: Quantifies average movement smoothness; higher values indicate more abrupt or irregular motion patterns associated with altered gait control

Description: Dispersion of jerk magnitude values around the mean
Clinical Relevance: Reflects the consistency of movement smoothness; elevated in unsteady or irregular gait

Description: Peak jerk magnitude within the window
Clinical Relevance: Captures the most abrupt acceleration change; sensitive to sudden movement transitions or foot strikes

Description: Minimum jerk magnitude within the window
Clinical Relevance: Represents the smoothest phase of motion within the walking segment

Description: Normalized sum of absolute acceleration values across all axes
Clinical Relevance: Global activity level descriptor; distinguishes active gait from low-movement or stationary states

Description: Number of times the X-axis signal crosses zero within the window
Clinical Relevance: Reflects oscillation frequency of lateral motion; indirectly related to step cadence

Description: Number of times the Y-axis signal crosses zero within the window
Clinical Relevance: Correlates with vertical oscillation frequency; sensitive to walking cadence changes

Description: Number of times the Z-axis signal crosses zero within the window
Clinical Relevance: Reflects the frequency of forward-backward acceleration reversals per window

Description: Zero crossings of the magnitude signal centered around its mean
Clinical Relevance: Captures the oscillation frequency of overall motion intensity around its average level

Description: Total energy of the medio-lateral acceleration signal
Clinical Relevance: Reflects the mechanical energy expended in lateral motion during the window

Description: Total energy of the vertical acceleration signal
Clinical Relevance: Proportional to vertical mechanical energy; increases with stride amplitude and speed

Description: Total energy of the antero-posterior acceleration signal
Clinical Relevance: Reflects propulsive energy expenditure in the walking direction

Description: Total energy of the resultant acceleration signal
Clinical Relevance: Combined kinetic energy proxy across all motion axes; increases consistently with gait speed

Description: Spectral amplitude at the frequency with the highest FFT magnitude
Clinical Relevance: Reflects the intensity of the most periodic component in the gait signal; typically corresponds to the fundamental step frequency

Description: Sum of squared FFT coefficients across all positive frequencies
Clinical Relevance: Represents the total frequency-domain energy of the motion signal

Description: Spectral power in the 4-6 Hz frequency band
Clinical Relevance: Captures energy in the Parkinsonian rest tremor frequency range; clinically relevant for tremor quantification

Description: Spectral power in the 0.5-3 Hz frequency band
Clinical Relevance: Associated with the fundamental locomotor rhythm; dominant during normal and slow walking

Description: Spectral power in the 3-8 Hz frequency band
Clinical Relevance: Overlaps with the freezing-of-gait detection band; second most important feature for gait classification

Description: Spectral power in the 8-15 Hz frequency band
Clinical Relevance: Associated with high-frequency impact components; may reflect heel strike intensity

Formula: H = sum(P_i * log2(P_i + eps)) * (-1); P_i = FFT_i / sum(FFT)
Description: Measure of disorder in the frequency distribution of the signal
Clinical Relevance: Lower in rhythmic and regular gait; higher in irregular or pathological walking patterns

Description: Frequency-weighted mean of the power spectrum
Clinical Relevance: Shifts toward higher frequencies with increasing gait speed; reflects the dominant oscillation rate

Description: Dispersion of spectral energy around the centroid frequency
Clinical Relevance: Reflects the bandwidth of the dominant gait rhythm; wider spread indicates less periodic motion

Description: Ratio of freeze-band power to locomotor-band power
Clinical Relevance: Key indicator used in Freezing of Gait detection; increases significantly during FoG episodes

Description: Spectral power in the locomotor frequency band (0.5-3 Hz)
Clinical Relevance: Energy of the rhythmic walking pattern; decreases during FoG episodes and in bradykinetic gait

Description: Spectral power in the freezing-of-gait frequency band (3-8 Hz)
Clinical Relevance: Increases relative to locomotor power during gait freezing; among the top-ranked features for gait classification

Description: Estimated step rate derived from peaks detected in a bandpass-filtered (0.5-3 Hz) magnitude signal
Clinical Relevance: Reduced cadence is a hallmark of bradykinetic gait in Parkinson's disease

Description: Standard deviation of the time intervals between consecutive detected steps
Clinical Relevance: Elevated values indicate temporal irregularity of the step rhythm; a sensitive marker of gait impairment

Formula: power(3-8 Hz) / (power(3-8 Hz) + power(0.5-3 Hz) + eps)
Description: Normalized contribution of the freeze band relative to combined locomotor and freeze band power
Clinical Relevance: Bounded between 0 and 1; facilitates cross-subject comparison of freezing tendency without scale dependency

Description: Number of steps detected by the accelerometer embedded digital signal processor within the 10-second window
Clinical Relevance: Direct cadence descriptor acquired at hardware level; complements software-estimated cadence from peak detection

Description: Total number of accelerometer data points recorded within the 10-second capture window
Clinical Relevance: Reflects the effective sampling rate achieved during acquisition; used for data quality control and normalization
